prize_parts.citation: for the theory of firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting, which showed how reallocation across firms shapes trade patterns and the gains from trade

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged from round 1: B048, credited to Melitz and Helpman. Round 1 moved me from B049 to B048, and the exchange has not reversed that. The case rests on three things. First, discovery: Melitz (2003) moved trade theory from the representative firm to selection into exporting and reallocation across firms, which is a new channel for the gains from trade. Second, maturity: more than twenty years of firm-level testing have supported the qualitative predictions (exporter premia, selection into export markets, within-industry reallocation after liberalisation). The disputes concern functional form and the size of welfare gains, not the mechanism. Third, credit: Melitz is the identifiable originator, and Helpman is the natural second name through the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple exporting-versus-FDI work and his earlier trade theory. The chair asked whether a citation limited to the selection and reallocation mechanism would suffice. For me it does, and it is the wording I now propose. It claims the theoretical mechanism and its testable implications, not priority over the whole firm-level empirical literature. I would not let field balance, the 2008 prize or thematic overlap with recent prizes count as evidence of merit. They bear on timing at most. Judged only on discovery, attribution and maturity, B048 remains my first choice. A close alternative, B001, would be credited at a real cost to attribution (Vishny), and the strongest claim it would have to defend is the contested one.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is unchanged. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum (and Yeaple) developed parallel firm-level facts and models and are outside the ballot entry. A two-name credit therefore leaves a priority question that the three-name cap cannot resolve and that careful wording only partly answers. Welfare-gain magnitudes depend on functional-form assumptions such as Pareto productivity. Helpman also appears in another package (B026, trade politics), which could split support or complicate framing. Finally, Redding's quantitative and spatial work is deliberately left out as a later strand, and that is a judgment call. If the committee decided the priority question for the empirical foundations was material and could not be handled by the citation, my preference between B048 and B001 would narrow. I would not move to B015 or B049 on that ground alone.

responses.point: Hassler prefers B001 and calls the gap with B048 small. He thinks creating a new field is somewhat more decisive than refining an established one, and he would word the citation around measurable institutions and established regularities, not the strong causal legal-origins reading.
responses.response: I take the wording proposal seriously. A citation that rests on the cross-country data, the research design and the finding that investor protection can be measured and co-varies with financial outcomes is more defensible than one resting on legal origin as a cause. I would also dispute the premise that B048 is only refinement. Melitz (2003) changed the unit of analysis in trade from the sector to the firm and made firm-level micro data the standard test bed, so it too founded a research programme. Even with your preferred wording, B001 still excludes Vishny, and its most visible claim is the contested part. B048's cost is the priority question around Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, which careful wording addresses at least partly. On those terms I still put B048 ahead, and I keep B001 as my first alternative because I see the gap as small.

responses.point: Friberg prefers B001 with moderate confidence. He concedes that B001 does not compete on identification credibility, and he rests the case on the field-creating contribution and the long period of testing. He lists B048 as his first alternative because of its cleaner two-name attribution and firm-level replication.
responses.response: Your candour moves the comparison toward a single question: how much weight identification and survival of the central claim should carry relative to field creation. I give them considerable weight, because a citation has to say what was established. You also note that the critiques are themselves part of maturity, and I agree that sustained scrutiny is evidence of a productive programme. But maturity does not settle which claim emerged intact. Because you rate B048 higher on attribution and replication, I think we differ mainly on the weight of field creation. You also work in trade and industrial organisation, which I note as proximity, not as a reason to discount your assessment.

responses.point: Strömberg prefers B001 and lists B049 and B048 as alternatives. He says that if the committee wants a cleaner identification record he would look at B049 or B048 and not at B001's rank. He would credit only Persson and Tabellini in B049.
responses.response: I accept that framing, and it is the one I used in round 1. If cleaner identification is the standard, I would choose B048 over B049, because cross-country identification of constitutional and electoral-rule effects is contested, and the 2024 institutions prize adds some thematic overlap. That is why I now rank B049 as a second alternative and not as my lead. Your Persson-Tabellini-only version of B049 is defensible on attribution, but it does not remove the identification problem. I am grateful that you list B048 as an alternative, since it suggests the disagreement is about weighting, not about the quality of the work.

responses.point: Krusell prefers B037 (Kiyotaki, Moore, Gertler), lists B048 as his first alternative, and would accept a two-name Kiyotaki-Moore version. He argues the 2022 prize overlap reduces marginal novelty and is not disqualifying.
responses.response: I agree that Kiyotaki and Moore are the clean core, and the two-name version removes the Gertler split with B040. I did not rank B037 in my opening, so my view is less developed than yours. My reservation is the one you state: the 2022 overlap reduces the marginal contribution, and the empirical identification of collateral channels is weaker than the theory's influence. I do not regard the overlap as disqualifying. I regard it as a smaller concern than the attribution problems I see elsewhere. B048 has both a cleaner two-name credit and more than twenty years of firm-level testing of its core predictions. I note that you list B048 first among your alternatives, and I would be glad to hear whether the two-name B037 would still rank ahead of B048 for you.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum priority question material enough that a citation limited to Melitz-Helpman and the selection mechanism is insufficient.
Whether Helpman's appearance on B026 reduces his claim on B048 or is only a reason to define the citation tightly.
How much the welfare-gain results depend on functional-form assumptions, and whether that weakens the claim of a robust discovery.

How much weight field-creating influence should carry against survival of the central claim, which is the main disagreement between B048 and B001. I may be underweighting influence, given my own earlier ranking of B001 second and B049 first.
My assessments rely on my recollection of the literature, and I have not independently verified any source.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to Melitz, Helpman, Redding, Shleifer, La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Persson, Tabellini or Besley appears in my supplied profile. My field is microeconomic theory and market design, which is not the field of the candidate I propose. I disclose that my profile records SSE affiliation alongside committee colleagues Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, which is not a candidate connection. Enflo noted my Lund affiliation and that I ranked B049 first in my opening. This is disclosed and not adjudicated, and I have since moved my preference away from B049. These disclosures are unchanged since round 1, and I do not adjudicate any colleague's conflicts.
